examples.question_text: Alex receives monthly take-home pay of $\$3200$ and spends $\$3450$ each month. Calculate the annual budget balance and state whether Alex is saving or dissaving.
examples.solution_text:
Convert both amounts to annual values.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Annual income} &= \$3200\times12\\&=\$38\,400\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Annual expenses} &= \$3450\times12\\&=\$41\,400\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Budget balance} &= \text{Income}-\text{Expenses}\\&=\$38\,400-\$41\,400\\&=-\$3000\end{aligned}$
Alex has an annual deficit of $\$3000$ and is dissaving.

examples.question_text: Priya receives take-home pay of $\$610$ per week. Her expenses are board of $\$180$ per week, transport of $\$45$ per week, entertainment of $\$110$ per fortnight, clothes of $\$210$ per month, and electricity of $\$240$ per quarter. Use $52$ weeks, $26$ fortnights, $12$ months and $4$ quarters per year. Prepare an annual budget and calculate her budget balance. State whether she is saving or dissaving.
examples.solution_text:
Convert each item to an annual amount.
$\text{Annual income}=\$610\times52=\$31\,720$
$\text{Board}=\$180\times52=\$9360$
$\text{Transport}=\$45\times52=\$2340$
$\text{Entertainment}=\$110\times26=\$2860$
$\text{Clothes}=\$210\times12=\$2520$
$\text{Electricity}=\$240\times4=\$960$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Total annual expenses}&=\$9360+\$2340+\$2860+\$2520+\$960\\&=\$18\,040\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Budget balance}&=\$31\,720-\$18\,040\\&=\$13\,680\end{aligned}$
Priya has an annual surplus of $\$13\,680$ and is saving.

examples.question_text: Noah receives take-home pay of $\$500$ per week for $40$ term weeks and $\$800$ per week for $12$ holiday weeks. He also receives $\$1200$ annually from a second income source. Throughout the $52$-week year, his expenses are rent of $\$250$ per week, groceries of $\$100$ per week, transport of $\$60$ per fortnight, and other living expenses of $\$200$ per month. He also contributes $\$1800$ annually to an investment from his take-home income. Include this contribution in his budget outgoings. Calculate his annual budget balance and state whether he is saving or dissaving.
examples.solution_text:
Calculate earnings for each part of the year, then add the second income.
$\text{Term earnings}=\$500\times40=\$20\,000$
$\text{Holiday earnings}=\$800\times12=\$9600$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Total annual income}&=\$20\,000+\$9600+\$1200\\&=\$30\,800\end{aligned}$
Convert the regular expenses to annual values and include the investment contribution.
$\text{Rent}=\$250\times52=\$13\,000$
$\text{Groceries}=\$100\times52=\$5200$
$\text{Transport}=\$60\times26=\$1560$
$\text{Other living expenses}=\$200\times12=\$2400$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Total annual outgoings}&=\$13\,000+\$5200+\$1560+\$2400+\$1800\\&=\$23\,960\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{Budget balance}&=\$30\,800-\$23\,960\\&=\$6840\end{aligned}$
Noah has an annual surplus of $\$6840$ and is saving.
